title: Mass Estimates of a Giant Planet in a Protoplanetary Disk from the Gap Structures
question: How can observed gap depths, together with disk temperature, constrain the mass of a giant planet embedded in a protoplanetary disk (applied to HL Tau and HD 169142)?

data.bands: Band 6 and Band 7 dust continuum (233 and 344 GHz central frequencies)

what.value: HD 169142 7 mm radial profile, aspect ratio ~0.1 and alpha=5e-4

evidence.quote: If we adopt the disk aspect ratio of $\sim 0.1$ and $\alpha=5\times10^{-4}$, as indicated by (cite: Osorio2014)

what.value: HL Tau ALMA continuum images (Band 6 and 7)

evidence.quote: HL Tau was observed during the 2014 Long Baseline Campaign of ALMA (cite: ALMA_HLTau)

recipe.method: Average Band 6 and 7 images azimuthally over 130°<PA<140° between 20 and 50 AU about the brightest pixel

recipe.goal: Solve for optical depth and temperature
recipe.method: Solve T_br = T(1-exp(-tau)) in both bands with tau7=tau6(nu7/nu6)^beta, for beta=1 and 2

recipe.goal: Estimate gap depth and aspect ratio, then planet mass
recipe.method: Ratio of tau max at 25 AU to min at 30 AU gives depth; T=55 K gives h~0.07; apply M_p/M_* formula
assumptions: c = 1 km/s (T/300 K)^1/2, stellar mass 1 Msun

answer_key.quantity: HL Tau gap depth at 30 AU
HL Tau aspect ratio at 25 AU

evidence.quote: we derive $h \sim 0.07$ as an estimate of the disk aspect ratio
we obtain the lower limit of the planet mass as $\sim 0.4~M_J$

not_stated_but_needed: Which archive FITS files (names, resolution, beam) were used for Band 6 and 7
Whether images were convolved to a common beam before taking the ratio
Coordinates of HL Tau and exact gap depth measurement procedure
Details of the chi2 spiral fit
missing_for_reproduction: Exact FITS files and beam handling
score_reason: Public images and simple analytic formulas, but profile extraction details are sparse.
rediscovery_reason: Public HL Tau images and a short analytic recipe with numeric results.
